title: APS Northwest Section — 2026 Annual Meeting
text:
Oregon Institute of Technology · Klamath Falls, Oregon · June 4–6, 2026
Welcome to the 2026 Annual Meeting of the APS Northwest Section! We are delighted to host you at OIT. Registration and the information desk are in the Auditorium Lobby (College Union, main floor).

Schedule and abstracts in the APS meeting archive



Thursday, June 4 — 4:00–5:00 p.m.: Registration, CU Auditorium Lobby — 5:00 p.m.: Welcome Reception, The Falls Taphouse
Friday, June 5 — OIT College Union, 8 a.m.–3:45 p.m.; banquet at Running Y Resort, 6 p.m. — Breakfast · Plenary sessions · Lunch · Parallel contributed sessions · Banquet
Saturday, June 6 — OIT College Union, 8 a.m.–3:30 p.m. — Breakfast · Plenary sessions · Lunch & poster session · Contributed sessions · Closing remarks

Registration and information desk — Auditorium Lobby, College Union main floor. Nametags and the LOC are here throughout the meeting.
Crater Lake Complex is directly up the stairs from the Auditorium Lobby. The poster session, Friday and Saturday lunches, and Friday’s parallel session room (CLC Mt Scott) are all here.



5:00 p.m. · The Falls Taphouse 2215 Shallock Ave, Klamath Falls, OR 97601
A 10-minute walk from the College Union. Food and drink — including a large selection of local microbrews — are available for purchase. We’ll be on the rooftop deck, weather permitting. Walking map on page 5.




Breakfast (8:00–9:00 a.m.) and lunch (12:15 p.m.) are provided each day at the College Union. All coffee breaks include refreshments in the Auditorium Lobby.
Dietary needs noted at registration will be accommodated.




6:00 p.m. reception · 6:45 p.m. dinner · Keynote to follow
Running Y Resort — Woodlands Ballroom 5500 Running Y Road, Klamath Falls, OR 97601 (541) 850-5500
Keynote: Matt Ginsberg (Google DeepMind) Physics and AI: Separating the Hype from the Reality
About 9 miles from OIT, 15 minutes by car. Take OR-140 toward Medford; Running Y is on the right. Carpooling is encouraged. Banquet tickets are available at the registration desk. Driving map on page 5.




OIT’s campus is compact — no lot is more than a five-minute walk from the College Union.
Avoid lots A, B, C, P, and Q (reserved for students and faculty during the week). Look for General Parking signs, or use:

Lots E and F — off Industrial Park Drive (large; usually plentiful)
Lots G and H — near Cornett Hall (large; usually plentiful)

Parking will be tighter on Friday (last day of class for OIT students) and easy on Saturday.

title: Northwest Section
text: The Northwest Section of the APS was officially founded in 1998 and now numbers over 1100 members and continues to grow. Its purpose is to facilitate the exchange of physics information and discussion among members living in the rather large area of the Pacific Northwest (primarily Alberta, British Columbia, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, Washington, and Wyoming & Alaska). The Section places emphasis on including students and physicists who work in education, research and in industry.

title: APS Northwest 2026
text:
Getting Here

By Car
Klamath Falls is located in Southern Oregon at the intersection of OR-140 and US-97.


By Plane
The nearest airport is in Medford, Oregon (MFR). The airport is about 70 miles from Klamath Falls.
Rental cars are available at the airport.
There are also buses that run between Medford and downtown Klamath Falls each day. The bus stops at the Medford airport, the Running Y, and downtown Klamath Falls, and costs about $25 each way. You can purchase tickets through Greyhound, Amtrak, and other carriers, but it is all the same route and carrier.
Other airports in the region include

Redmond, Oregon — RDM, about 120 miles (near Bend, Oregon)
Redding, California — RDD, about 120 miles
Reno/Tahoe, Nevada — RNO, about 250 miles
Portland, Oregon — PDX, about 290 miles
Sacramento, California — SMF, about 290 miles



By Train
Amtrak’s scenic Coast Starlight train connects Los Angeles to Portland and Seattle, and passes through Klamath Falls twice a day (8 a.m. northbound, 10 p.m. southbound).

section: Things to Do In and Around Klamath Falls
text:
Things to Do In and Around Klamath Falls
Klamath Falls has a pleasant and walkable downtown with several breweries and coffee roasters. You can explore Western art and Native American artifacts at the Favell Museum. Opportunities for hiking, kayaking, and mountain biking abound in the surrounding area, with nearby Moore Park offering lakefront trails and Cascade views. (Expect pleasant June weather with highs in the 70s–80s°F and cool evenings.)
You can also …

Play golf at the Running Y — Oregon’s only Arnold Palmer-designed signature golf course
Attend the Oregon Shakespeare Festival in Ashland, Oregon
Visit Crater Lake National Park
Hike and spelunk at Lava Beds National Monument
Watch for birds along the Klamath Basin Birding Trail, at the Lower Klamath National Wildlife Refuge, or at the Upper Klamath National Wildlife Refuge (all part of the Pacific Flyway)
